46821.subject: Zoology
46821.text: Which of the following is not considered as a secondary messenger?
46821.sol: Acetylcholine is not considered as a secondary messanger. Cholinergic nerve fibres release acetylcholine. It has excitatory effect on the skeletal muscles and excitatory or inhibitory effect at the other sites.

47555.sol: A₂(g)+2 B(g) C(g)+Q k J Obviously, the forward reaction is exothermic. Thus, according to Le-Chatelier's principle, the lower is temperature, greater would be the yield of ammonia. Also, the forward reaction occurs with decrease in number of gaseous molecules. Thus, according to Le-Chatelier's principle an increase in pressure, will shift the equilibrium in a direction in which the number of gaseous molecules decreases. In other words high pressure will favour the formation of products.

108661.sol: For 1 mole of an ideal gas, the molar heat capacities are related by Mayer's relation: C_ p,m - C_ v,m = R . For n moles of the gas, the total (extensive) heat capacity at constant pressure is C_P = nC_ p,m and at constant volume is C_V = nC_ v,m . Substituting these into the relation gives: C_P n - C_V n = R Multiplying the entire equation by n , we get: C_P - C_V = nR Answer: C_P - C_V = nR

116329.subject: Chemistry
116329.text: If 10 moles of dinitrogen and 15 moles of dihydrogen are mixed in a closed vessel to synthesize ammonia, what is the maximum number of moles of ammonia that can be formed?
116329.sol: The balanced chemical equation for the synthesis of ammonia is: N ₂( g ) + 3 H ₂( g ) 2 NH ₃( g ) According to the reaction, 1 mole of N ₂ requires 3 moles of H ₂ . For 10 moles of N ₂ , the required moles of H ₂ = 10 3 = 30 moles . Since only 15 moles of H ₂ are available, H ₂ is the limiting reagent. The amount of product formed depends on the limiting reagent. From the balanced equation, 3 moles of H ₂ produce 2 moles of NH ₃ . Therefore, 15 moles of H ₂ will produce 2 3 15 = 10 moles of NH ₃ . Answer: 10

123660.sol: This leads to the formation of haploid gametes. The key features of meiosis are as follows: Meiosis involves two sequential cycles of nuclear and cell division called meiosis I and meiosis II but only a single cycle of DNA replication. It also regulates sexual behaviour and regulating the period of puberty.

128781.sol: Erythrocytes or red blood cells (RBC) are the most abundant of all the cells in blood. A healthy adult man has, on an average , 5 million to 5.5 million of RBCs mm–3 of blood . RBCs are formed in the red bone marrow in the adults. RBCs are devoid of nucleus in most of the mammals and are biconcave in shape. They have a red colored, iron containing complex protein called haemoglobin, hence the color and name of these cells. A healthy individual has 12-16 gms of haemoglobin in every 100 ml of blood. 129133.subject: Zoology
129133.text: Which one of the following is a matching pair?
options: Lubb - sharp closure of AV valves at the beginning of ventricular systole
Dup - sudden opening of semilunar valves at the beginning of ventricular diastole
Pulsation of the radial artery - valves in the blood vessels
Initiation of the heart beat - Purkinje fibres
129133.sol: The gradually increasing contraction of ventricular muscles during systole first causes the closure of bicuspid and tricuspid valves (AV valves), producing a low-pitched "lubb" sound. Later, it causes the opening of the semilunar valves of systemic and pulmonary aorta. At the end of ventricular systole, semilunar valves shut, producing the second, louder heart sound, the "dup". Thus each heart beat is accompanied by a "lubb-dup" sound.

129833.subject: Zoology
129833.text: What is the average Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV) in healthy adults?
129833.sol: Tidal Volume (TV): Volume of air inspired or expired during a normal respiration. It is approx. 500 mL., i.e., a healthy man can inspire or expire approximately 6000 to 8000 mL of air per minute. Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV): Additional volume of air, a person can inspire by a forcible inspiration. This averages 2500 mL to 3000 mL. Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV): Additional volume of air, a person can expire by a forcible expiration. This averages 1000 mL to 1100 mL.

130401.sol: Calcium Ions (Ca²⁺): Binds to troponin, leading to the displacement of tropomyosin. Troponin: Binds to calcium ions, causing a conformational change that affects tropomyosin. Tropomyosin: Shifts to expose the myosin-binding sites on actin, allowing contraction. Myosin ATPase: Enzyme that hydrolyzes ATP to provide energy for muscle contraction.

130485.sol: According to NCERT, a cup-shaped bone called the patella covers the knee ventrally. Therefore, 'X' is the patella. The ankle bones are known as tarsals. In human females, menstruation is repeated at an average interval of about 28/29 days, and the cycle of events starting from one menstruation till the next one is called the menstrual cycle.

133076.sol: Neanderthal man was the first human fossil discovered in 1856 having a cranial capacity of 1400 cc. African man (Australopithecus) was discovered in 1924 having a cranial capacity of 300-500 cc . 95221.subject: Botany
95221.text: Passage cells are thin walled cells found in
options: Phloem elements that serve as entry points for substance for transport to other plant parts
Testa of seeds to enable the emergence of growing embryonic axis during seed germination
The central region of style through which the pollen tube grows towards the ovary
Endodermis of roots facilitating rapid transport of water from cortex to pericycle
95221.sol: The innermost layer of the cortex is called endodermis. It comprises a single layer of barrel-shaped parenchyma cells without any intercellular spaces. In roots, thick-walled endodermal cells are interrupted by thin-walled passage cells or transfusion tissue. Passage cells facilitate the transportation of water from cortex to pericycle. The passage cells are thin-walled and are usually located opposite the protoxylem.

97201.sol: Short day plants will only flower if they are exposed to a short period of daylight and long periods of darkness. If the dark period is interrupted, the plant will not flower. Hence, short-day plants are also called long night plants, e.g., rice, soyabean, etc.

6a7a1ff8c687f7da0a3121b1.text: A point charge Q is placed at the origin (0, 0, 0) of a 3D coordinate system. Two points A and B are located at (2, 3, 3 ) m and (x, 5 , 2 ) m respectively. If the work done in moving a test charge from point A to point B is zero, the positive value of the unknown coordinate x is:
6a7a1ff8c687f7da0a3121b1.sol: The work done in moving a test charge from point A to point B is zero, which implies that the potential difference between the two points is zero. Thus, both points must lie on the same equipotential surface, meaning they are at the same distance from the origin. The distance of point A from the origin is: r_A = 2^2 + 3^2 + ( 3 )^2 = 4 + 9 + 3 = 16 = 4 m The distance of point B from the origin is: r_B = x^2 + ( 5 )^2 + ( 2 )^2 = x^2 + 5 + 2 = x^2 + 7 m Equating the distances: r_A = r_B 4 = x^2 + 7 16 = x^2 + 7 x^2

6a7a1ff8e0fd89bc9cee90e8.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff8e0fd89bc9cee90e8.text: The dimensional formula of a physical quantity is given by [M L^2 T⁻² A⁻¹] . Which of the following combinations of SI units represents this quantity?
6a7a1ff8e0fd89bc9cee90e8.sol: The dimensional formula for electric potential (Volt) can be found using the relation Potential = Work / Charge. [ Volt ] = [M L^2 T⁻²] [A T] = [M L^2 T⁻³ A⁻¹] Multiplying this by the dimension of time (second), which is [T] : [ Volt second ] = [M L^2 T⁻³ A⁻¹] [T] = [M L^2 T⁻² A⁻¹] This matches the given dimensional formula. Answer: Volt second

6a7a1ff867483731376de12b.text: A block rests on the horizontal floor of an elevator that is accelerating upwards at 2 m s ⁻² . The effective acceleration due to gravity is g' = g + a_e = 10 + 2 = 12 m s ⁻² . The normal force exerted by the floor on the block is N = m g' = 12m . The kinetic friction acting on the block is f_k = N = 0.5 12m = 6m . The horizontal deceleration of the block relative to the elevator is: a = f_k m = 6 m s ⁻² . Using the kinematic equation v^2 = u^2 - 2as with final velocity v = 0 relative to the elevator: 0 = (6)^2

6a7a1ff84cadc2dfc6c04db9.text: In a Young's double slit experiment, the widths of the two slits are in the ratio n : 1 (where n > 1 ). The visibility of the interference fringes on the screen is given as 0.8 . Assuming that the intensity of light from a slit is directly proportional to its width, what is the value of n ? (Fringe visibility V is defined as V = I_ max - I_ min I_ max + I_ min )
6a7a1ff84cadc2dfc6c04db9.sol: Let the widths of the two slits be w₁ and w₂ . We are given w₁ w₂ = n . Since the intensity is directly proportional to the slit width ( I w ), the ratio of intensities is: I₁ I₂ = n I₁ = n I₂ The maximum and minimum intensities in the interference pattern are: I_ max = ( I₁ + I₂ )^2 = ( n + 1)^2 I₂ I_ min = ( I₁ - I₂ )^2 = ( n - 1)^2 I₂ The fringe visibility V is given by: V = I_ max - I_ min I_ max + I_ min Substitute the expressions for I_ max and I_ min : I_ max - I_ min = 4 n I₂ I_ max + I_ min = 2(n + 1) I₂ V
